rules.statement: Every OpenID protocol endpoint must return an `x-fapi-interaction-id` response header: echo the request's value only when it is a canonical hyphenated UUID (RFC 4122), keeping its exact text and letter case, and otherwise (absent, empty or not a UUID) return a newly generated UUID.
rules.why: FAPI 1.0 Part 1 §6.2.1-11 requires it and the OpenID conformance suite checks it. Echoing an arbitrary client string would carry untrusted input into logs and downstream systems.
rules.check: Look for code that sets `x-fapi-interaction-id` by copying the request value without checking that it is a UUID, code that changes the letter case of an echoed UUID, and protocol endpoints that leave the header out.

rules.statement: Set the `x-fapi-interaction-id` response header in one filter on the protocol endpoint group, before the next delegate runs, so that success results, error results and requests refused by environment or rate-limit filters all carry it.
rules.why: If the header is set after the endpoint runs, or only on some endpoints, some responses go out without it, and clients correlate every call they make.
rules.check: Look for the header being set per endpoint or after `next` is awaited, for new protocol endpoints added outside the group that has the filter, and for the filter registered outside the rate-limit and environment filters, so that refused requests skip it.
